source_caption:
Rutger Hauer found the original script written by David Peoples to be too technical and "overwritten" (what he called "opera talk") and felt it did not fit the emotional, intimate climax of the character's death, leading him to rewrite and drastically shorten the speech the night before filming. 

He created and added the final, most memorable lines himself: "All those moments will be lost in time, like tears in rain. Time to die", as a way to show Batty’s acceptance of his mortality. He didn't tell director Ridley Scott about the changes beforehand, but after the take, the crew was allegedly moved to silence and then applause. 

The monologue from Blade Runner (1982) is regarded as one of the greatest ad-libbed moments in cinema history.

source_details.title: Blade Runner
source_details.synopsis: Blade Runner is a 1982 science fiction film directed by Ridley Scott from a screenplay by Hampton Fancher and David Peoples. Starring Harrison Ford, Rutger Hauer, Sean Young, and Edward James Olmos, it is an adaptation of the 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? by Philip K. Dick. The film is set in a dystopian future Los Angeles of 2019, in which synthetic humans known as replicants are bio-engineered by the powerful Tyrell Corporation to work on space colonies. When a fugitive group of advanced replicants led by Roy Batty (Hauer) escapes back to Earth, former cop Rick Deckard (Ford) is recalled to hunt them down.
